## Abstract

Direct solvers for linear algebraic systems scale cubically in the problem's dimension, rapidly becoming intractable for large-scale problems, while sparse factorization may still require quadratic storage du fill-in.
Krylov techniques avoid these costs by needing only a routine that computes a matrix-vector product, iteratively building a subspace from which the solution is obtained.
`LightKrylov` is a Fortran package providing a suite of such Krylov methods along with an easy-to-use high level API based on `abstract types`.
It is primarily intended for applications where the linear operator of interest is only available implicitly via a matrix-vector subroutine and enables users to maximally re-use existing components of their code base (including parallelization), thus requiring a minimal set of changes without sacrificing computational performance.
